requirements: The core contributions of the paper 'Mirror Speculative Decoding: Breaking the Serial Barrier in LLM Inference' have been reproduced.

sub_tasks.requirements: The heterogeneous GPU-NPU serving environment, tensor-parallel configuration, interconnects, and reproducibility settings described in Section 4.1 and F.1 have been established.

The heterogeneous compute topology (8 GPUs for target, 8 NPUs for draft, grouped into pairs across nodes with die-to-die and inter-node interconnects) has been provisioned as described in Section F.1.
Code has been implemented that provisions and detects 8 GPU devices for target execution and 8 NPU devices for draft execution, with device handles exposed to the serving stack.

verification.spec: Import the device provisioning module and call the initialization routine. Assert that it returns/exposes exactly 8 GPU device handles for the target and 8 NPU device handles for the draft (or matching abstractions when running on emulated hardware). Verify handles are accessible to the serving stack via a documented API.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that organizes the 8 M2 Ultra nodes into 4 groups of 2, with each intra-group pair linked via Thunderbolt 5 (up to 120 Gbps) and inter-group traffic routed through the high-speed network fabric.

verification.spec: Inspect the cluster topology configuration. Assert the 8 nodes are partitioned into 4 groups of 2, that intra-group links are labeled/configured for Thunderbolt 5 (120 Gbps), and inter-group links route through the high-speed network fabric. Verify via configuration file or topology query API.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that uses the UltraFusion die-to-die interconnect (up to 2.5 TB/s) inside each M2 Ultra so that its dual-die package appears as a single logical GPU/NPU pair to the runtime.

verification.spec: Query the runtime device enumeration on an M2 Ultra node. Assert each dual-die package is presented as a single logical GPU device and a single logical NPU device (rather than two separate dies), consistent with UltraFusion abstracting the die-to-die interconnect.

sub_tasks.requirements: The tensor-parallel groupings for target (GT=8, Megatron-style) and draft (GD=8, SPD-style) have been configured and instantiated as process/device groups.
Code has been implemented that creates a Megatron-style TP process group of size GT=8 over the GPU devices, with column-parallel W_qkv/W_o in MHA and column/row-parallel W1/W2 in the MLP.

verification.spec: Import the target sharding module. Initialize with GT=8 and inspect the constructed process group and per-layer weight shards. Assert (a) TP group size equals 8, (b) W_qkv and W_o are column-parallel, (c) W1 is column-parallel and W2 is row-parallel in the MLP, and (d) each transformer block emits exactly two all-reduce collectives (one after attention, one after MLP).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that creates an SPD-style device group of size GD=8 over the NPU devices, pinning track g to NPU g with a resident weight shard for its segment.

verification.spec: Import the draft sharding module. Initialize with GD=8 and inspect the constructed device group. Assert (a) group size equals 8, (b) each track g in {1..8} is bound to NPU g, and (c) each track holds a resident, non-replicated weight shard for its segment (verify shard shapes differ from full weights).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that establishes an AllReduce collective backend within each device group (separate GPU-side and NPU-side collectives) with no cross-group coupling in the collective plan.

verification.spec: Inspect the collective-communication setup code. Assert two disjoint process groups are created: one for the target GPUs and one for the draft NPUs. Assert that AllReduce calls within a Mirror-SD step reference only the appropriate group's communicator (no communicator spans both device types). Verify by grepping/introspecting the group membership dict and confirming intersection is empty.

sub_tasks.requirements: The default serving configuration used across all Mirror-SD experiments (batch size 1, speculative window gamma=7, early exit at half depth, top-kappa=8, bf16 token channel) has been instantiated as a reproducible configuration.
Code has been implemented that fixes the evaluation batch size to B=1 and the speculative window length to gamma=7 for all main SpecBench runs.

verification.spec: Load the default SpecBench evaluation config used for the main results and assert config.batch_size == 1 and config.gamma (speculative window length) == 7. Additionally, invoke the runner's argument parser with default flags and confirm the effective values propagated to the decoding loop are B=1 and gamma=7.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that sets the early-exit layer l_e to 1/2 of the target model's total depth and configures top-kappa=8 for the token channel.

verification.spec: For each supported target (Qwen3-14B, Qwen3-32B, Mistral-24B, OPT-66B), load the Mirror-SD config and assert that config.early_exit_layer == floor(target.num_hidden_layers / 2) and config.top_kappa == 8. Verify via a small forward-pass integration test that the hook fires at exactly the configured layer index.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that exposes both greedy (T=0) and stochastic (T=1) decoding modes with identical decoding hyperparameters applied to Mirror-SD and all baselines.

verification.spec: Run the same prompt through Mirror-SD and at least one baseline (e.g., vanilla SD) at T=0 and T=1. Assert (a) both decoding modes are selectable via a temperature argument, (b) at T=0, repeated runs on the same seed produce identical outputs (deterministic), (c) at T=1, outputs vary across seeds, and (d) the temperature and sampling settings passed to Mirror-SD and baselines are identical for a given task.

sub_tasks.requirements: Determinism and reproducibility controls (pinned interconnects, disabled frequency scaling, fixed seeds/configs from SpecBench) have been enabled for timing measurements.
Code has been implemented that pins interconnect routes/topology (Thunderbolt 5 pairings and fabric links) so that the communication path is invariant across runs.

verification.spec: Inspect the run configuration / launch script. Assert it declares an explicit static topology: fixed pairing of the 8 nodes into 4 groups of 2 over Thunderbolt 5, with an explicit inter-group fabric routing table. Verify a topology config file (YAML/JSON) is loaded and its route entries are deterministic (no dynamic route discovery flags).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that disables CPU/GPU/NPU dynamic frequency scaling (governor set to performance / DVFS locked) for all latency measurements.

verification.spec: Inspect the benchmarking launcher and confirm it sets CPU governor to 'performance' (or macOS equivalent power-mode lock) and disables GPU/NPU DVFS (e.g., pinned clocks via vendor tool or sysctl). Assert a pre-run check reads back current governor/DVFS state and aborts the benchmark if not locked.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that loads SpecBench's released configs and seeds so that prompts, sampling settings, and pre/post-processing are identical across methods.

verification.spec: Import the SpecBench harness wrapper. Assert it loads configuration from the released SpecBench repo (https://github.com/hemingkx/Spec-Bench) including its prompt files, sampling settings (temperature, top-p), and fixed random seeds. Run the loader twice and assert identical prompt ordering and identical seed values across invocations.

sub_tasks.requirements: Timing instrumentation that measures compute, collectives, and rendezvous overhead end-to-end has been implemented so that wall-time speedups can be reported.
Code has been implemented that measures per-step wall-time including target compute, draft compute, TP AllReduce collectives, and both early-exit and final rendezvous overheads.

verification.spec: Instrument the per-step timer with subcomponent hooks: (target_compute, draft_compute, tp_allreduce, early_exit_rendezvous, final_rendezvous). Run one Mirror-SD step end-to-end and confirm the aggregated per-step wall-time equals the sum (or max on parallel paths) of all five components, and that none of the five components is missing or zero when they should be active.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes end-to-end wall-time speedup as (target-only AR decoding time) / (method decoding time) on identical prompts for each SpecBench task.

verification.spec: For a fixed SpecBench task and prompt set, measure wall-time T_AR of target-only autoregressive decoding and T_method of Mirror-SD on identical prompts and identical generation lengths. Verify the reported speedup equals T_AR / T_method (within floating-point tolerance) by comparing the computed value against the metric emitted by the runner.

sub_tasks.requirements: The SpecBench framework and its constituent tasks (translation, summarization, QA, math reasoning, RAG, MT-Bench) have been set up with the paper's prompts, sampling and evaluation protocol.
The SpecBench evaluation framework itself has been obtained and integrated as the harness for wall-time benchmarking.
Code has been implemented to acquire the open-source SpecBench framework (Xia et al., 2024b) including its standardized prompts, pre/post-processing utilities, released configurations, and seeds.

verification.spec: Verify that the SpecBench framework is available in the repo: check that a `specbench` (or equivalent) directory/module is present containing prompts, pre/post-processing utilities, released config files (yaml/json), and seed specifications. Programmatically import the SpecBench loader and confirm it exposes tasks such as translation, summarization, QA, math_reasoning, RAG, and multi-turn conversation with associated prompt files.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that invokes SpecBench's released configs and fixed random seeds so evaluation runs are reproducible across baselines and Mirror-SD.

verification.spec: Run the SpecBench evaluation script twice back-to-back with the same target/draft and no code changes. Assert that (a) generated token sequences per prompt are identical for greedy decoding (T=0), and (b) reported per-task speedup numbers agree within 1% run-to-run. This confirms the released configs and seeds are actually applied.

sub_tasks.requirements: Sampling and decoding hyperparameters used at evaluation time match the paper's protocol.

Code has been implemented to run every SpecBench task under both greedy decoding (temperature T=0) and stochastic decoding (temperature T=1) using identical decoding hyperparameters across Mirror-SD and all baselines.

verification.spec: Invoke the SpecBench runner for one task (e.g., Translation) once with T=0 and once with T=1, and confirm both runs complete and produce speedup outputs. Diff the effective decoding hyperparameters passed to Mirror-SD and to at least one baseline (e.g., EAGLE3): assert they are identical except for the temperature field, ensuring hyperparameter parity across methods.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the main benchmarking runs use fixed batch size B=1 and speculative window length gamma=7 as specified in Section 4.1.

verification.spec: Load the main benchmark config used to produce Table 1 and Figure 4. Assert batch_size == 1 and speculative_window_length (gamma) == 7. Fail if either value differs.

sub_tasks.requirements: The two evaluation metrics defined in Section 4.1 are computed correctly from benchmark runs.

Code has been implemented to compute end-to-end wall-time speedup over target-only autoregressive decoding on the same hardware, including compute, collectives, and rendezvous overhead, and to report it as a speedup factor per task.

verification.spec: Run the repo's benchmark harness on a small target model over a fixed SpecBench task with (i) target-only autoregressive decoding and (ii) Mirror-SD decoding, using identical prompts and seeds. Assert the harness returns a wall-time speedup factor per task, computed as (baseline_wall_time / mirror_wall_time), that the timing includes model forward compute, collective/sync ops, and rendezvous overhead (verified by inspecting the timer scope in the code), and that the returned speedup for the same run is deterministic across two calls.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to compute acceptance length E[A_t] as the expected number of tokens accepted per speculative window, averaged across steps and prompts, and to report mean +/- std per task as in Figure 3b.

verification.spec: Run the benchmark harness's acceptance-length computation on a small deterministic example where the number of accepted tokens per step is known by construction (e.g., mock the target/draft to always accept 3 out of gamma=7 tokens). Assert the reported E[A_t] equals 3.0 and that the reported std is ~0, and separately assert on a stochastic case that the returned value is the arithmetic mean over all steps and prompts and includes a std field.

sub_tasks.requirements: Server-scale target models Qwen3-14B, Qwen3-32B, Mistral-24B, and OPT-66B have been obtained and deployed with Megatron-style tensor parallelism over 8 GPUs including early-exit hooks.
All four target models have been acquired from public checkpoints and loaded for inference.
Code has been implemented to load the Qwen3-14B target model checkpoint (Yang et al., 2025) via a HuggingFace-compatible loader.

verification.spec: Call the repo's target-model loader with identifier 'Qwen/Qwen3-14B' and verify it returns a HuggingFace-compatible model object whose config.num_hidden_layers and config.hidden_size match the published Qwen3-14B values, and that a forward pass on a short dummy input returns logits of shape [B, T, vocab_size].

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to load the Qwen3-32B target model checkpoint via a HuggingFace-compatible loader.

verification.spec: Call the repo's target-model loader with identifier 'Qwen/Qwen3-32B' and verify it returns a HuggingFace-compatible model object whose config matches the published Qwen3-32B (num_hidden_layers, hidden_size), and that a forward pass on a short dummy input returns logits of the expected shape.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to load the Mistral-Small-3 24B target model checkpoint.

verification.spec: Call the repo's target-model loader with identifier 'mistralai/Mistral-Small-24B-Base-2501' and verify it returns a HuggingFace-compatible model whose config matches Mistral-Small-24B (approximately 24B parameters), and that a forward pass on a short dummy input returns logits with the expected shape.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to load the OPT-66B target model checkpoint (Zhang et al., 2022).

verification.spec: Call the repo's target-model loader with identifier 'facebook/opt-66b' and verify it returns a HuggingFace-compatible OPT model whose config.num_hidden_layers and config.hidden_size match published OPT-66B values. Given the 66B model size and H100 memory constraints, allow loading in bfloat16 or with device_map='auto'; verify a forward pass succeeds on a short dummy input.

sub_tasks.requirements: For each target model, tokenizer, vocabulary size |V|, transformer depth N, hidden width H_T, and layer-count metadata are exposed to downstream sharding and scheduling code.

verification.spec: For each supported target (Qwen3-14B, Qwen3-32B, Mistral-24B, OPT-66B), load the model config and assert a metadata dict exposing keys: tokenizer, vocab_size (|V|), num_layers (N), hidden_size (H_T). Assert these values match the model card values (e.g., Qwen3-14B: 40 layers, H=5120, vocab=151936 or as declared in the config) and are accessible to the sharding scheduler.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Megatron-style tensor-parallel wrapping of each target model has been implemented with G_T=8 GPU shards.
Code has been implemented that shards MHA weights W_qkv as column-parallel and W_o as row-parallel across the 8 GPU target group.

verification.spec: Introspect the MHA layer's parameter partitioning on the 8-GPU target group. Assert W_qkv is column-parallel: its output feature dimension is sharded to size H/8 per rank while input dim is full. Assert W_o is row-parallel: its input feature dimension is sharded to H/8 per rank while output dim is full. Verify by checking parameter .shape on rank 0 versus the unsharded reference shape.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that shards the MLP with column-parallel W_1 and row-parallel W_2 across the 8 GPU target group.

verification.spec: Introspect the MLP layer's parameter partitioning on the 8-GPU target group. Assert W_1 (up-projection) is column-parallel: its output dimension is sharded (intermediate/8 per rank). Assert W_2 (down-projection) is row-parallel: its input dimension is sharded (intermediate/8 per rank). Verify by shape inspection against the unsharded reference.

sub_tasks.requirements: Each transformer block performs exactly two AllReduce collectives per forward step (one after attention and one after MLP), matching the standard Megatron TP contract.

verification.spec: Wrap the AllReduce collective with a global counter. Run one forward pass of a single transformer block on the 8-GPU target group and assert the counter increments by exactly 2 (one after MHA, one after MLP). Extend to N blocks and assert counter == 2*N. This confirms the standard Megatron TP contract of two collectives per block.

sub_tasks.requirements: The tensor-parallel target produces bit-identical (or within numerical tolerance) next-token logits compared to the single-device reference forward on a small validation batch, confirming correctness of the sharding.

verification.spec: Load a small target (or a small proxy transformer with the same TP wrapper) both in a single-device configuration and in the GT=8 Megatron-style TP configuration. Run a forward pass on identical input tokens. Assert that next-token logits from the TP configuration match the single-device reference within numerical tolerance (e.g., max absolute diff < 1e-3 in fp32 or < 1e-2 in bf16).

sub_tasks.requirements: KV-cache layout is compatible with existing inference stacks (per-shard KV storage aligned with the Megatron partitioning) so that speculative verification can teacher-force accepted tokens without reshuffling.

verification.spec: Run a Mirror-SD step that accepts a prefix of length A_t=3, then invoke the next step which must teacher-force those 3 accepted tokens through the target. Assert (a) the KV-cache tensors on each of the 8 target GPUs remain sharded along the head/hidden dim matching Megatron partitioning, (b) no reshuffle/all-gather of KV occurs between steps, and (c) the teacher-forced logits match a reference run that never used speculation for the same accepted tokens (within fp16/bf16 tolerance).

sub_tasks.requirements: Early-exit hooks and the shared LM head at the mid-depth layer have been wired into every target model.
Code has been implemented to configure the early-exit layer index l_e = floor(N/2) for each target model (Qwen3-14B, Qwen3-32B, Mistral-24B, OPT-66B) based on its total depth N.

verification.spec: Load the Mirror-SD config for each target (Qwen3-14B, Qwen3-32B, Mistral-24B, OPT-66B), inspect the resolved early-exit layer index, and assert it equals floor(N/2) where N is the target's transformer depth (e.g., N=40 -> l_e=20 for Qwen3-14B). Fail if any target's l_e deviates from mid-layer.

sub_tasks.requirements: A hook at layer l_e applies the target LM head W_LM to the intermediate hidden state h_t^{(l_e)} and returns a proxy distribution p^{(l_e)}(.|y_<t, x) = Softmax(W_LM h_t^{(l_e)}) without terminating the forward pass.

verification.spec: Instantiate a small target model and register the Mirror-SD early-exit hook at layer l_e. Run a forward pass on a dummy sequence and assert (a) the hook captures the intermediate hidden state h_t^{(l_e)}, (b) the returned proxy distribution equals Softmax(W_LM @ h_t^{(l_e)}) to within 1e-5 by comparing against a manual computation using the target's LM head, and (c) the forward pass continues beyond layer l_e (i.e. hidden states at layers > l_e are populated).

sub_tasks.requirements: After the early-exit projection fires, the target continues execution through layers l_e+1, ..., N in the same step to produce the final distribution p^{(N)} used for verification.

verification.spec: Instantiate a small target model with Mirror-SD's early-exit machinery enabled, run one decoding step, and confirm that within the same forward invocation both (a) the early-exit proxy distribution p^{(l_e)} is emitted, and (b) the model returns a final distribution p^{(N)} computed by continuing through all layers l_e+1, ..., N. Assert that p^{(N)} matches a reference vanilla forward pass to within 1e-5 max abs error.

sub_tasks.requirements: The early-exit hook is non-destructive: disabling it yields target outputs bit-identical to the vanilla forward pass, verifying the hook does not perturb the final distribution p^{(N)}.

verification.spec: Load a small target model twice: once with the early-exit hook attached (but with the token-channel emission side-effect disabled/no-op), and once without. Run both on identical inputs with identical seeds and assert that the final-layer logits are bit-identical (torch.equal) or within numerical rounding (max abs diff < 1e-6). This confirms the hook is non-destructive to p^{(N)}.

sub_tasks.requirements: Deployment configuration binds each target model to the 8-GPU M2 Ultra target group with reproducibility controls.
Configuration files specify G_T=8 GPUs as the target device group for every target model, with per-rank memory-fit checks passing for Qwen3-14B, Qwen3-32B, Mistral-24B, and OPT-66B.

verification.spec: Parse the deployment/config files for each target model and assert G_T == 8 (tensor-parallel world size). Then attempt to instantiate the sharded target on the available hardware and assert per-rank memory footprint fits within device memory budget for all four targets.

sub_tasks.requirements: The deployed target performs an autoregressive greedy generation smoke test on a fixed prompt and reproduces the reference token sequence, verifying end-to-end model loading, TP sharding, and early-exit-disabled path.

verification.spec: With early-exit disabled and greedy decoding, generate 32 tokens for a fixed seed prompt on the sharded target and assert the emitted token IDs match a reference sequence produced by the same model loaded in a single-GPU non-sharded reference implementation (or a stored golden output).

sub_tasks.requirements: The Mirror-SD scheduler co-schedules target (GT=8 GPUs, Megatron TP) and draft (GD=8 NPUs, SPD sharding with 2 segment-boundary all-reduces) as depicted in Figure 2, realizing the overlap budget in the latency law of Section 3.4 / Appendix C.
Target-side Megatron-style tensor-parallel sharding across GT=8 GPUs with per-block two-collective structure has been implemented.

Code has been implemented that shards the target transformer across GT=8 GPU ranks using Megatron-style tensor parallelism, with column-parallel W_qkv and W_o in MHA and column-parallel W_1 / row-parallel W_2 in the MLP.

verification.spec: Import the target model wrapper and instantiate it with GT=8 TP ranks. Inspect the MHA and MLP submodules and assert that W_qkv and W_o are ColumnParallelLinear/RowParallelLinear (or equivalent) with column-parallel W_qkv+W_o, and that MLP W_1 is column-parallel and W_2 is row-parallel. Verify per-rank parameter shapes match H/GT and 4H/GT partitioning.

sub_tasks.requirements: Each target transformer block issues exactly two tensor-parallel all-reduce collectives per forward pass (one after MHA, one after MLP), matching the Megatron sync pattern depicted in Figure 2.

verification.spec: Hook the TP all-reduce primitive (e.g., monkey-patch torch.distributed.all_reduce or the collective wrapper) with a counter, run one forward pass of a single target transformer block with GT>=2, and assert exactly 2 all-reduce calls are recorded per block (one at end of MHA, one at end of MLP).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the target's TP all-reduce message size per rank equals M_T = B*S_T*H_T / G_T and its cost is modeled as T_allreduce(M_T; G_T) = alpha*log(G_T) + beta*M_T, consistent with Appendix C.

verification.spec: Call the latency-model utility that computes T_allreduce given (B, S_T, H_T, G_T, alpha, beta). Assert per-rank message size equals B*S_T*H_T/G_T and returned cost equals alpha*log(G_T) + beta*(B*S_T*H_T/G_T) for several parameter settings.

sub_tasks.requirements: Heterogeneous co-scheduling of the target (GPU group) and draft (NPU group) with independent, non-coupled collective domains has been implemented.

Code has been implemented that places the target on GT=8 GPUs and the draft on GD=8 NPUs as separate process/device groups, with all target compute and target collectives confined to the GPU group and all draft compute and draft collectives confined to the NPU group.

verification.spec: Inspect the Mirror-SD launcher: assert that target parameters and target collective groups have device_type 'gpu' (or cuda:*) across 8 ranks, and draft parameters and draft collective groups have device_type 'npu' (or ane/mlx) across 8 ranks. Verify no parameter tensor of target lives on an NPU device and vice versa.

sub_tasks.requirements: Draft and target all-reduces occur within their own device groups with no cross-collective coupling (matching the Figure 2 note that 'AllReduce Draft + Target' bands are visual shorthand for two independent collectives).

verification.spec: Instrument both target and draft collective wrappers with tagged group IDs. Run one Mirror-SD step and assert that every all-reduce carries either the target-group tag or the draft-group tag, and that no collective spans both groups (no cross-group coupling).

sub_tasks.requirements: A concurrent execution scheduler has been implemented so that, after early exit, target-suffix computation (layers l_e+1..N on GPUs) runs in parallel with draft branch-complete generation (on NPUs) within the same Mirror-SD step.

verification.spec: Time-stamp start/end events of target-suffix computation (layers l_e+1..N) and draft branch-complete generation within one Mirror-SD step. Assert the two intervals overlap in wall-clock time (max(start_target_suffix, start_draft_gen) < min(end_target_suffix, end_draft_gen)).

sub_tasks.requirements: Per-step latency measurement and the Mirror-SD piecewise latency law from Section 3.4 / Appendix C have been implemented and validated.

Code has been implemented that measures T_target^{1:l_e}, T_target^{l_e+1:N}, T_draft^{gen}(gamma), T_rv^{(ee)}, and T_rv^{(fv)} per Mirror-SD step, including compute, collectives, and rendezvous overhead.

verification.spec: Run one Mirror-SD step and dump the per-step profiler record. Assert the record contains numeric fields T_target_1_le, T_target_le1_N, T_draft_gen_gamma, T_rv_ee, T_rv_fv, each > 0 and covering compute + collectives + rendezvous overhead.

sub_tasks.requirements: The step latency computation implements the piecewise law T_Mirror = T_target^{1:l_e} + T_rv^{(ee)} + max(Delta, T_draft^{gen}(gamma)) + T_rv^{(fv)} with Delta = T_target^{l_e+1:N}, so that draft generation is fully hidden when T_draft^{gen}(gamma) <= Delta.

verification.spec: Call the step-latency computation with synthetic component values where T_draft_gen < Delta and where T_draft_gen > Delta. Assert output equals T_target_1_le + T_rv_ee + max(Delta, T_draft_gen) + T_rv_fv with Delta=T_target_le1_N in both regimes.

sub_tasks.requirements: Measured Mirror-SD step latency matches the piecewise law of Equation (10) within tolerance across a sweep of gamma, exhibiting a near-zero-slope regime while T_draft^{gen}(gamma) <= Delta and a linear-in-excess regime beyond.

verification.spec: Sweep gamma in {1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8} on MT-Bench with Qwen3-14B target and 0.6B SS draft. Record measured T_Mirror per step and fit against the piecewise law T_Mirror = C + max(Delta, T_draft_gen(gamma)). Assert R^2 > 0.9 and that the slope of T_Mirror vs gamma is near zero (< 20% of the slope in the excess regime) for gamma values where measured T_draft_gen(gamma) <= Delta, and grows approximately linearly beyond.

sub_tasks.requirements: Cross-accelerator rendezvous is implemented as a lightweight token channel whose transfer cost is negligible relative to compute.

Code has been implemented so that Mirror-SD performs exactly two token-level GPU<->NPU exchanges per step, one at early exit l_e and one at final verification N, each carrying O(B*kappa) IDs and log-probabilities.

verification.spec: Instrument the GPU<->NPU token channel. Run one Mirror-SD step and assert exactly 2 cross-device transfers occur: one at layer l_e (early exit) and one at layer N (final verification). Assert each payload size is O(B*kappa) bytes (contains at most B*kappa token IDs plus B*kappa log-probabilities).

sub_tasks.requirements: Measured rendezvous transfer time T_xfer^{(ee)} + T_xfer^{(fv)} is on the microsecond scale, negligible relative to millisecond-scale target/draft compute, as claimed in Section 3.3.

verification.spec: Time the two rendezvous transfers over 100 Mirror-SD steps with B=1, kappa=8. Assert mean (T_xfer_ee + T_xfer_fv) is under 1 ms while mean target-step compute is > 10 ms, i.e. rendezvous is <10% of compute.

sub_tasks.requirements: Scheduler-side integration of draft capacity scaling with the overlap budget is verified: enlarging gamma below the overlap budget adds no marginal critical-path latency.

Instrumentation reports the overlap budget Delta = T_target^{l_e+1:N} and the draft generation time T_draft^{gen}(gamma) each Mirror-SD step and flags whether draft work is fully hidden (T_draft^{gen}(gamma) <= Delta).

verification.spec: Run several Mirror-SD steps with varying gamma. Assert the per-step log output contains fields Delta and T_draft_gen_gamma, plus a boolean 'overlap_hidden' set to (T_draft_gen_gamma <= Delta). Verify the flag flips correctly across steps where the inequality changes.

sub_tasks.requirements: In the regime T_draft^{gen}(gamma) <= Delta, measured T_Mirror equals T_target + T_rv within tolerance, confirming zero marginal cost of increasing gamma up to the overlap budget.

verification.spec: Select a small gamma (e.g., 2) so that measured T_draft_gen <= Delta. Time full Mirror-SD steps and compare with T_target + T_rv (measured separately by running target only + timing rendezvous). Assert |T_Mirror - (T_target + T_rv)| / T_target < 0.10.

depends_on: Draft Model Training with Speculative Streaming

sub_tasks.requirements: All comparison baselines (vanilla SD, Medusa, Hydra, EAGLE-2/3, Recycling, PLD, SpS, REST, Lookahead) have been set up via SpecBench with the paper's configurations for Qwen3-14B/32B, Mistral-24B, and OPT-66B targets.
SpecBench framework has been integrated for baseline execution with standardized prompts, pre/post-processing, sampling settings, and released configs/seeds for fair comparison.
Code has been implemented to clone/install the SpecBench framework (Xia et al., 2024b) with the released configs and seeds used by the paper.

verification.spec: Run the setup script that clones the SpecBench repository (https://github.com/hemingkx/Spec-Bench) at the pinned commit and installs its Python dependencies. Assert `import specbench` (or equivalent module import per SpecBench README) succeeds and the released config directory containing seeds/configs is present.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to load the SpecBench standardized prompts and pre/post-processing pipelines for all six tasks (translation, summarization, QA, math reasoning, RAG, multi-turn conversation).

Verify mean absolute relative error |T_pred - T_obs| / T_obs is under 10% across at least 50 steps, confirming the latency decomposition faithfully models observed behavior.

sub_tasks.requirements: Measurements confirm the draft-dominated regime: when T_draft^gen(gamma) > Delta, observed T_Mirror scales as T_target^{1:l_e} + T_draft^gen(gamma) + T_rv, matching the second branch of Equation (10).

Also verify that in this regime T_Mirror scales linearly with gamma (slope > 0), unlike the hidden-draft regime.

Fit the same regression to vanilla SD over the same gamma range and verify slope is significantly positive (slope / mean_latency > 0.15 per unit gamma). Report the ratio of Mirror-SD slope to vanilla-SD slope.

sub_tasks.requirements: Per-step time-saved and speedup formulas from Appendix C (Delta_T = min{Delta, T_draft^gen(gamma)} - T_rv; piecewise speedup S = T_SD / T_Mirror) are validated against measured wall-time.

Verify mean relative error between empirical and predicted time-saved is under 15% over at least 50 matched steps.

sub_tasks.requirements: The strict-speedup condition T_rv < min{Delta, T_draft^gen(gamma)} is empirically verified to hold in the reported Mirror-SD configurations, consistent with Mirror-SD achieving the reported 2.8x-5.8x wall-time speedups on SpecBench.

verification.spec: For each reported Mirror-SD configuration (Qwen3-14B, Qwen3-32B with 0.6B SS draft, gamma=7), measure Delta = T_target^{l_e+1:N}, T_draft^gen(gamma), and T_rv over at least 100 steps on SpecBench prompts. verification.spec: Call the serial-latency helper with mocked T_draft and T_target values; assert the returned step latency equals their sum within numerical tolerance, matching Eq. (5).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements the low-bandwidth token channel that emits only the top-kappa candidate tokens and their log-probabilities from the early-exit layer ell_e (Eq. (7), Section 3.1).

verification.spec: Feed a synthetic intermediate hidden state h_t^(ell_e) with known softmax; call the token-channel builder with kappa=8; assert the message contains exactly kappa (token_id, logprob) pairs corresponding to the top-kappa entries and no other payload.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements branch-complete rollouts: given the top-kappa early-exit roots, the draft prepares speculative continuations for every prefix length r <= gamma from each candidate v_i (Eq. (8), Section 3.1).

verification.spec: Run the branch-complete rollout routine with kappa=2, gamma=3 on a mock draft; assert the produced tensor has shape [kappa, gamma, ...] and that path (i, r) starts with root v_i and has length r+1.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements the accepted-prefix length A_t as the largest r in {0,...,gamma-1} such that all draft tokens y_hat match the target's greedy/stochastic tokens y^targ, per Section 3.1.

verification.spec: Provide synthetic (y_hat, y_targ) sequences; assert A_t returned equals largest r where the prefixes agree, matching the formula around image [220 x 19].

sub_tasks.requirements: Code produces the correction token c_{t+tau} at index tau = A_t + 1 when A_t < gamma, following Section 3.1.

verification.spec: With A_t=2 and gamma=5, run the correction extractor over mock target distributions; assert it returns tau=3 and the token argmax p^(N)(.|y_<t+2).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements the reuse condition Pi_t^+ in Paths_tau(T_t): reuse fires iff the corrected accepted prefix appears as a root-to-depth-tau path in the hypothesis tree.

verification.spec: Construct a small hypothesis tree with known paths; call the reuse predicate with (a) a Pi_t^+ that matches an existing path and (b) one that does not; assert True and False respectively.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements the operational next-window selection rule of Mirror-SD, choosing between reuse of a precomputed branch and recomputation of speculation based on the reuse criterion, as specified in Section 3.1.

verification.spec: Drive the next-window selector with three cases (reuse match, no-match forcing recompute, and A_t==gamma with no correction); assert branch chosen equals the rule described around image [376 x 49] and that the committed output equals y^targ_{t+1:t+A_t}.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements the SS draft-step count formula J = ceil(gamma / eta_bar) (or equivalent inequality) that bounds the number of internal draft steps needed to materialize a gamma-token window, per Section 3.2.

verification.spec: Call the draft-step counter with gamma=7 and per-step token yields eta_j; assert the returned J satisfies sum_{j=1..J} eta_j >= gamma and J is minimal, matching the formula around image [110 x 28].

sub_tasks.requirements: Code implements the target suffix time T_target^{ell_e+1:N} = sum_{ell=ell_e+1}^{N} c_ell used as the overlap budget Delta in the Mirror-SD latency model (Section 3.4).

verification.spec: Given per-layer times c_ell for a depth-N target and an early-exit index ell_e, assert the overlap-budget helper returns sum(c_{ell_e+1..N}) within 1e-9.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the Mirror-SD verification routine correctly identifies when the corrected prefix (accepted tokens plus correction token) matches a precomputed root-to-depth path in the hypothesis tree T_t, triggering the reuse branch instead of recomputing speculation.
